parole.significato: Synonym of turnip cake (often particularly referring to stir-fried preparation popular in South East Asia)
parole.testo: From Teochew 菜頭粿 /菜头粿 (cai³ tao⁵ guê²) and Hokkien 菜頭粿 /菜头粿 (chhài-thâu-kóe).

parole.significato: To malinger, to skive, to shirk one's duties (especially, military duties) by feigning illness or reporting sick.
parole.testo: From Teochew 臭 (cao³, “dirty, ill-reputed”) + 經 /经 (gêng¹, “to evade; to pass the buck”).

parole.significato: A kind of steamed rice cake originating in Teochew cuisine, served with preserved radish (chai po).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Teochew 水粿 (zui² guê²) or Hokkien 水粿 (chúi-kóe).

parole.significato: Roasted chestnuts.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Teochew 侯栗 (gao⁶ lag⁸, “chestnut”).

parole.significato: Fortunate, lucky.
parole.testo: From Teochew 興 /兴 (hêng¹, “fortunate”) or Hokkien 幸 (hēng, “fortunate”). Compare Thai เฮง (heng), Khmer ហេង (heeng), Vietnamese hên.

parole.significato: Phew!, thank goodness; expressing relief, e.g., when an extremely unlucky outcome has been avoided.
parole.testo: From Teochew 興啊 /兴啊 (hêng¹ a⁷) or Hokkien 幸啊 (hēng--a). By surface analysis, heng (“lucky”) + ah (used for emphasis).

parole.significato: Synonym of chao keng (“to malinger, to shirk military duties by reporting sick”).
parole.testo: Clipping of chao keng, from Teochew 臭 (cao³, “dirty, ill-reputed”) + 經 /经 (gêng¹, “to evade; to pass the buck”).

parole.significato: Someone who avoids work, military duties or other responsibilities by constantly reporting sick; a malingerer.
parole.testo: keng + -ster, the first element is a clipping of chao keng, from Teochew 臭 (cao³, “dirty, ill-reputed”) + 經 /经 (gêng¹, “to evade; to pass the buck”).

parole.significato: A Teochew dish of flat rice sheets in a soy sauce broth and an array of braised meats (offal, tongue, rinds, pork belly…
parole.testo: From Teochew 粿汁 (guê² zab⁴). Compare Thai กวยจั๊บ (guai-jáp) / ก๋วยจั๊บ (gǔai-jáp).

parole.significato: Synonym of silver needle noodles.
parole.testo: From Teochew 米篩目／米筛目 (bhi² tai¹ mag⁸), with the first element reanalyzed as the word mee, meaning “noodles”, from Hokkien 麵／面 (mī).

parole.significato: A person of Chaoshan heritage.
parole.testo: From Teochew 潮州 (dio⁵ ziu¹). See also Hokkien 潮州 (Tiô-chiu). Doublet of Chaozhou.

parole.significato: A Southeast Asian noodle dish made from flat rice noodles, soy sauce, chili, prawns and other common stir-fry ingredien…
parole.testo: From either or both Teochew 炒粿條 /炒粿条 (ca² guê² diou⁵) or Hokkien 炒粿條 /炒粿条 (chhá-kóe-tiâu). See also kway teow. Compare Malay kuetiau, Indonesian kwetiau, Burmese ကွေ့တီယို (kwe.tiyui), Khmer គុយទាវ (kuy tiəw), Thai ก๋วยเตี๋ยว (gǔai-dtǐao), Vietnamese hủ tiếu.

parole.significato: A lecher, a pervert.
parole.testo: From either or both Hokkien 痴哥 (chhi-ko) and Teochew 痴哥 (ci¹ go¹).

parole.significato: Deep; profound; complex.
parole.testo: Borrowed from either Hokkien 深 (chhim, “deep”) or Teochew 深 (cim¹, “deep”).

parole.significato: Speech or writing marked by overly complex vocabulary.
parole.testo: From cheem + -ology on analogy of -inology words like criminology and terminology in which the -in- belongs to the Latin oblique stem, the former from either Hokkien 深 (chhim, “deep”) or Teochew 深 (cim¹, “deep”).

parole.significato: Strong (used as a modifier after kopi (“coffee”)).
parole.testo: From either Hokkien 厚 (kāu, “thick”) or Teochew 厚 (gao⁶, “thick”), influenced in spelling by Mandarin Pinyin.

parole.significato: a person who traces his/her ancestry to Hailufeng or the surrounding area
parole.testo: Possibly either Hailufeng Min 海陸豐 /海陆丰 or Teochew 海陸豐 /海陆丰. Compare Indonesian Hailokhong, Dutch Hailokhong. Doublet of Hailufeng.

parole.significato: A type of flat rice noodles, commonly used in Hokkien and Teochew cuisine.
parole.testo: From either or both Hokkien 粿條 /粿条 (kóe-tiâu) and Teochew 粿條 /粿条 (guê² diao⁵). Compare Malay kuetiau, Indonesian kwetiau, Burmese ကွေ့တီယို (kwe.tiyui), Khmer គុយទាវ (kuy tiəw), Thai ก๋วยเตี๋ยว (gǔai-dtǐao), Vietnamese hủ tiếu.

parole.significato: Hardened snot, booger.
parole.testo: From either or both Hokkien 鼻屎 (phīⁿ-sái) and Teochew 鼻屎 (pin⁷ sai²).

parole.significato: A kind of spring roll.
parole.testo: Borrowed from either or both Teochew 薄餅 /薄饼 (boh⁸ bian²) and Hokkien 薄餅 /薄饼 (po̍h-piáⁿ). Compare Thai เปาะเปี๊ยะ (bpɔ̀-bpía), Vietnamese bò bía, Malay popia.

parole.significato: An exclamation of annoyance or exasperation.
parole.testo: From Teochew and Hokkien. Ultimate origin uncertain: first element equivalent to Hokkien 我 (óa, “my”) + lau, possibly from 老爸 (lāu-pē, “father”). Alternatively, a shortening of Hokkien 我老的 (óa lāu--ê, literally “my elderly [someone, e.g., father]”), from which the alternative forms wah lau eh and wa
